comment: Catalogue of local models the appliance can fetch at setup time, and of the
llama.cpp runtime backends it can run them on. Staged here and installed by
the 070 hook to /etc/safi/local-models.json. Read by safi-browser-setup.py
(to render the model picker) and by safi-model-fetch (to download and
verify). Both consumers parse this file, so the format is deliberately flat
JSON rather than code shared through an import path: safi-model-fetch runs
on stdlib python before the app venv is known to be healthy.
Every url is pinned to a digest-verified artefact. sha256 is mandatory and
a mismatch aborts the fetch and never starts the server -- a model fetched
over the network is otherwise a supply-chain hole in a product whose audit
kv_bytes_per_token is the f16 KV cache cost at the configured context
window: 2 (K and V) * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * 2 bytes. For Qwen3 that
is 144 KiB/token for 4B and 8B (36 layers), 160 KiB/token for 14B (40) and
256 KiB/token for 32B (64). Cross-checked against llama.cpp's reported KV
size for Qwen3-0.6B (112 KiB/token) and Qwen3-8B (144 KiB/token) at 8192.
model_root_comment: Installed weights live at <model_root>/<model id>/<file>. Stated here rather than hardcoded so safi-model-fetch (which writes) and the app (which reports what is installed) cannot drift apart. 'file' is given per model for the same reason: deriving it from the url's basename is a convention, and a convention shared across two codebases is a drift waiting to happen.
overhead_comment: Reserved for SAFi + MariaDB + page cache, added on top of weights + KV when deriving min_ram. 2.5 GiB.

cpu.label: CPU only
cpu.on_iso_comment: The 070 hook already installs this tarball's contents into /opt/safi/bin, so a CPU fetch must not download it again. The asset entry is kept so a rebuild can re-derive the pinned digest from one place.

vulkan.label: AMD GPU (Vulkan / RADV)
vulkan.home_comment: safi-model-fetch installs the llama-server archive here and points the systemd unit's LD_LIBRARY_PATH at it, the same way CUDA builds land in /opt/safi/cuda.

backend_note: The CPU tarball ships on the ISO; a CUDA box pays the ~765 MB backend
download once, at setup. The Vulkan (AMD) backend is a 31 MB download that
runs on the Mesa RADV driver, which the ISO installs from Debian -- no
ROCm stack and no /dev/kfd needed, which is what makes it reliable on the
kernel trixie ships (6.12 even drives Strix Halo / gfx1151 iGPUs for this).
A CUDA backend needs BOTH assets above. llama.cpp split the CUDA runtime out
of the server archive at b11205, so fetching only llama-server yields a
build whose ggml-cuda.so cannot resolve libcudart, which fails at the first
GPU layer load rather than at startup -- hence the two-entry list and the

models.label: SAFi-Qwen3.8-27B
models.summary: Flagship for AMD Strix Halo. Native MTP speculative decoding roughly doubles its token rate on a Vulkan iGPU; ~10 tok/s sustained on a Radeon 8060S with the stock Vulkan build (measured on the EVO-X2). Third-party GGUF because Qwen publish no GGUFs for this model.
models.kv_bytes_per_token_comment: Hybrid attention: only the 16 full-attention layers of the 64 produce KV (Qwen3.8-27B is 48 linear + 16 full). Q8 cache measured ~2.45 GiB at 32K ctx; at the shipped 64K window that doubles to ~4.9 GiB, and the f16 figure used below is 4.3 GB (4.0 GiB).
models.context_size_comment: Per-model, not catalogue-global: this entry overrides context_size so the 27B runs a 64K window (YaRN 2x its native 32K, see llama_args) while smaller models keep the 8192 default. KV at 64K is 4.3 GB of the RAM/VRAM floors below.
models.reasoning_comment: Qwen3 supports thinking but defaults to --reasoning off to avoid spending thousands of chain-of-thought tokens per turn and timing out.
models.min_vram_comment: 16.8 GB weights + 4.3 GB KV at the configured 64K ctx (65536 * 65536). On an APU this is met through the TTM GTT pool (raised boot param), not the small UMA carve-out.
models.optimized_for_comment: On an AMD GPU that fits it, this model is marked recommended ahead of a strictly larger generic model, so a Vulkan Strix Halo box pre-selects the engine this ISO is tuned around.
models.llama_args_comment: Verified against the b11205 Vulkan build: native MTP draft head (no second model), flash attention, quantized KV, and YaRN at 2x for the 64K window. --spec-draft-n-max 3 is the measured optimum (5 dropped decode from ~10 to ~7.6 tok/s as draft acceptance collapsed). Reasoning effort comes from the reasoning fields above, not a hardcoded unit flag.

models.label: SAFi-Qwen3-Coder-30B
models.summary: MoE coder: 30B total but ~3B active per token, so decode is memory-bandwidth cheap rather than compute bound. Measured ~65 tok/s on the Radeon 8060S with the stock Vulkan build on the EVO-X2, roughly 2x the dense Qwen3.8-27B. Instruction/coding tuned, non-thinking, and has no MTP draft head.
models.kv_bytes_per_token_comment: 48 layers, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128, f16: 2 * 48 * 4 * 128 * 2 bytes.
models.llama_args_comment: No MTP head on the coder, so no speculative flags. Flash attention plus quantized KV as on the 27B; -np 1 -b 2048 -ub 512 match the single-user tuning measured on the EVO-X2. Reasoning stays off: it is an instruction/coder model, not a thinking one.

models.label: SAFi-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
models.summary: Qwen3.6 MoE: 35B total / ~3B active, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention, ships a native MTP head so speculation needs no separate draft model. Measured 77.7 tok/s on the Radeon 8060S (EVO-X2, Vulkan b11205) with --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3; the same file without the MTP flags drops to 58.6, so the flags are load-bearing.
models.kv_bytes_per_token_comment: Only the 10 full-attention layers of the 40 produce context KV (30 are Gated DeltaNet with constant state): 2 * 10 * 2 KV heads * 256 head_dim * 2 bytes = 20480 B/tok. KV at the shipped 32K ctx is just 0.67 GB.
models.min_vram_comment: 22.66 GB weights + 0.67 GB KV (20480 B/tok at 32768 ctx) = 23.33 GB, far under the Strix Halo 53 GiB TTM pool.
models.context_size_comment: Doubled from 32768 after a 34,768-token request overflowed the 32K window: KV is only 20480 B/tok (10 attention layers), so 64K costs just 0.67 GB more. Well inside the model native 262144 and the Strix Halo 53 GiB pool.
models.reasoning_comment: Qwen3.6 supports thinking but ships here as a non-thinking engine via --reasoning off; no chain-of-thought tokens before each answer.
models.llama_args_comment: Native MTP speculative decoding at depth 3 hit 77.7 tok/s on the Radeon 8060S with the stock Vulkan b11205 bundle (58.6 spec-less, 60.8 at n_max 5). Flash attention plus quantized KV, matching the rest of the catalogue.

models.label: SAFi-Llama3.1-8B
models.summary: More capable general-purpose model; needs substantially more CPU time than the small options.
models.min_vram_comment: 0 = runs acceptably on CPU; a GPU only makes it faster.

retired.qwen3-0.6b: Dropped from the picker. Q4_K_M shipped at 484 MB but leaked the ---REFLECTION--- contract on 6/6 runs and called a real fiduciary tool on 0/6, so it could neither be reasoned with nor audited. A box that can hold it can hold the 4B.
